statement: A robot stands in the top-left cell of an m × n grid and wants to reach the bottom-right cell. At each move it goes one cell right or one cell down.
Each cell of grid is 0 (free) or 1 (an obstacle). The robot can never enter a cell that holds an obstacle.
Return the number of different paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell that avoid every obstacle.

examples.explanation: The obstacle in the centre blocks every path through it. Only two paths are left: along the top row then down the right column, or down the left column then along the bottom row.
The starting cell itself is an obstacle, so there is no path at all.
